name: Mathematical and Quantitative Methods
solves: estimate a causal effect from data not produced by experiment
predict the outcome when several parties choose strategically

tools.name: Ordinary least squares (Gauss–Markov theorem)
tools.does: gives the best linear unbiased estimator
hypotheses: the model is linear in parameters
errors have zero mean given the regressors
errors are uncorrelated with equal variance

tools.name: Instrumental variables
tools.does: estimates an effect when the regressor is confounded
hypotheses: the instrument affects the outcome only through the regressor
monotonicity, for a local average effect

tools.name: Difference-in-differences
tools.does: estimates an effect from before-after change against a comparison group
hypotheses: the groups would have followed parallel trends

tools.name: Nash equilibrium existence theorem
tools.does: guarantees an equilibrium in mixed strategies

name: Microeconomics

decide whether decentralised exchange wastes anything

tools.name: Utility maximisation and demand
tools.does: derives demand from preferences and a budget

tools.name: First welfare theorem
tools.does: says a competitive equilibrium is Pareto efficient

tools.name: Revenue equivalence theorem
tools.does: says standard auctions yield the same expected revenue
hypotheses: independent private values from one distribution
the lowest type expects zero surplus

name: Macroeconomics and Monetary Economics
solves: explain long-run growth of output per head
predict how a whole economy responds to a shock or a policy rate

tools.name: Solow growth model
tools.does: gives steady-state output per worker from saving and population growth
hypotheses: saving, population growth and technical progress are exogenous

tools.name: Dynamic stochastic general equilibrium model
tools.does: simulates responses of the economy to shocks
hypotheses: a representative agent, or few agent types

tools.name: Taylor rule
tools.does: describes a policy rate from inflation and the output gap
hypotheses: estimates of the output gap and neutral rate exist
it describes behaviour and is not an optimum by itself

tools.name: Comparative advantage (Ricardian model)

hypotheses: factors move within but not between countries

tools.name: Heckscher–Ohlin theorem
tools.does: predicts exports from relative factor abundance

tools.name: Gravity model of trade

name: Financial Economics
solves: price a risky asset
value a claim whose payoff depends on another price
choose a mix of risky holdings

tools.name: Capital asset pricing model
tools.does: gives expected return from market risk
hypotheses: investors care only about mean and variance
unlimited borrowing and lending at the risk-free rate

tools.name: Black–Scholes formula
tools.does: prices a European option
hypotheses: the price follows geometric Brownian motion with constant volatility
continuous trading with no transaction costs

tools.name: Modigliani–Miller theorem
tools.does: says firm value does not depend on financing mix

tools.name: Mean-variance portfolio selection
tools.does: finds the lowest-risk mix for a target return
hypotheses: means and covariances of returns are known

name: Public Economics

tools.name: Samuelson condition
tools.does: gives efficient provision of a public good
hypotheses: the good is non-rival and non-excludable

tools.name: Tax incidence analysis

hypotheses: elasticities of supply and demand are known
